reviewer.executor: GPT-6 Luna module reviewer with Codex primary source review

reviewScope.criterion: Frozen compound core facts and concrete source-backed errors; not exhaustive answer accuracy

factReviews.reason: Answer gives the exact prepare_method/url/headers/cookies/body/auth/hooks order and explains why auth follows the prepared request fields and precedes hooks.

Q1 only names prepare_request as a stage. Across the answer and follow-ups, it does not state the merge of request/session cookies or the merge_setting/merge_hooks behavior for request and Session headers, params, auth and hooks; the frozen compound fact is therefore not conveyed.
Q4 accurately covers elapsed, hook dispatch, historical/current cookie extraction, redirect processing, and non-stream content consumption; Q1 places adapter.send in the request flow.

Q6 accurately explains trust_env-controlled proxy/no_proxy resolution and explicit proxy setdefault precedence; Q1 names environment settings generically. The answer set does not give the REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/CURL_CA_BUNDLE condition or the complete merge of proxies, stream, verify and cert with Session settings, so the compound fact is only partial.
Q4 describes redirect handling and history but never states the max_redirects check or TooManyRedirects boundary; no other answer supplies this fact.
Q11 accurately states the 4xx/5xx raise boundary and that ok is not equivalent to status 200, including 3xx. It does not connect Response.__bool__ to ok, which is part of the frozen compound fact.
Q9 correctly distinguishes the uncached stream, consumed-but-not-cached sentinel and bytes cache; it covers cached slicing and StreamConsumedError on a consumed uncached stream.

Q19 correctly identifies charset_normalizer as a declared runtime dependency and chardet as optional, but does not enumerate the four direct runtime dependencies or identify the use_chardet_on_py3 optional group. References to urllib3/idna for compatibility aliases do not establish the full dependency claim.

findings.claim: A streamed object with a known length gets Content-Length; otherwise it gets Transfer-Encoding: chunked.
findings.reason: The branch tests `if length`, not whether length is known. A known zero length is falsey and therefore selects chunked; the answer omits this boundary while stating the rule generally.

findings.claim: It describes body-position recording, response-hook registration, and counter reset as occurring only in the branch where last_nonce already exists.
findings.reason: Only building and adding the preemptive Authorization header is conditional on last_nonce. tell/position handling, registering both handle_401 and handle_redirect, and setting num_401_calls=1 happen on every __call__, including the first challenge request. This changes the described first-request retry behavior.

findings.claim: The runtime no-op exists to avoid repeated assertions on a hot path.
findings.reason: The source comment gives a narrower reason: `is_prepared` is a runtime no-op to avoid AssertionError while serving as a TypeIs predicate for static checking. It does not say the helper avoids repeated assertions or that this is a hot-path optimization; the answer turns an unsupported performance rationale into fact.

limitations: Assistant source review is not independent human blind review.
Review covers all 20 main answers and all nested follow-ups against the fixed source revision; it is not exhaustive of every factual nuance.
No model/network calls and no upstream project code execution.

primaryReview.method: Primary agent checked every frozen fact disposition and all retained findings against the pinned source, read every mitt answer and all Requests main answers, and verified run/output/fingerprint bindings. The module reviewers read every answer and nested follow-up.
primaryReview.deduplication: Repeated identical claim within one question counts once, with occurrence locations retained.
